item.title: GM wants drivers to take their eyes off the road by 2028
item.description: GM plans to debut eyes-off driving in the Cadillac Escalade IQ by 2028, but safety testing reveals how long distracted drivers take to regain control.
item.content:encoded:
Would you feel comfortable watching a movie while your car cruises down the highway at 70 mph? General Motors is betting that someday you will. The automaker plans to introduce technology in 2028 that could let drivers take their hands off the steering wheel and their eyes off the road. That means you could potentially answer emails, watch a show or attend a virtual meeting while your vehicle handles the driving.

The technology is expected to debut in the Cadillac Escalade IQ electric SUV. However, GM still has plenty to prove before drivers can safely look away from traffic. The company is testing how people react when a vehicle suddenly needs their attention. That research could help GM determine how much warning drivers need before safely taking control.

Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com.

IKEA TURNS TO DRIVERLESS SEMIS WITH NOBODY IN THE CAB

GM already offers Super Cruise, a hands-free driving system available on more than 20 models across Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC and Buick. It can manage steering, acceleration and braking on compatible roads under certain conditions. However, drivers must continue watching the road and remain ready to take control.

The next version of Super Cruise would remove that constant attention requirement when the eyes-off feature is active. GM plans to introduce it on compatible highways before eventually expanding to other roads. The system will use lidar, radar and cameras to monitor its surroundings. Turquoise lights on the dashboard and exterior mirrors will signal when eyes-off driving is available and active. GM says the technology could arrive as early as 2028. However, the launch depends on further development, safety testing and other requirements. Availability will also depend on state laws.

GM's ambitions are also growing. On Oct. 21, the company announced plans to bring autonomous highway driving to its full-size SUVs and light-duty pickup trucks, including gas-powered vehicles. Those vehicles represent some of GM's biggest sellers. However, the automaker has not announced when the technology will reach those additional models.

Before asking drivers to trust a vehicle with their safety, GM wants to understand what happens when people stop concentrating on driving. At its Global Technical Center in Warren, Michigan, hundreds of volunteers have climbed into real GM vehicles, including the Cadillac Lyriq. However, instead of driving onto an actual highway, they enter an immersive simulator that recreates different road conditions. Researchers can introduce sudden traffic changes, construction zones and hazardous situations.

Meanwhile, sensors monitor drivers' eye movements, heart rates and stress responses. The tests help GM understand how people behave when the technology encounters something unexpected. GM also tests its automated driving technology on closed courses and public roads with trained safety drivers. According to the company, its simulation tools can reproduce the equivalent of 100 years of driving in a single day. That gives engineers opportunities to study dangerous situations without exposing everyday drivers to those risks.

Here's something I didn't expect to see in automotive safety research. GM is asking some participants to play Candy Crush while researchers study their reactions. The game creates an engaging distraction. Players become focused on improving their scores, which gives researchers a way to measure what happens when they must suddenly shift their attention back to driving. According to reporting by The Associated Press, Maureen August, a senior manager at GM Research & Development, explained that the game helps researchers draw participants into an activity before interrupting them.

That interruption is especially important. Consider how long it takes to understand what's happening around you after you've been concentrating on your phone. Now consider making that adjustment while sitting behind the wheel of a moving SUV. At 70 mph, a vehicle travels roughly 103 feet every second. Even a five-second delay means it covers more than 500 feet. That's a lot of highway to travel while someone figures out why the car needs help.

WHAT HAPPENS IF THE WAYMO COMPUTER FAILS?

This may be the biggest question surrounding GM's plans. What happens when an automated vehicle encounters a situation it cannot safely handle? Perhaps there's debris blocking the highway. Maybe road markings disappear during construction. An unexpected maneuver by another driver could also create a dangerous situation.

GM's engineers are studying how much warning drivers need before taking control. Researchers also examine whether people understand the system's alerts and feel comfortable trusting the technology. However, an eyes-off system must be designed around the possibility that someone cannot respond immediately. That's why the vehicle's ability to handle unexpected conditions and safely manage a failed takeover becomes especially important. GM has not yet publicly detailed every situation its planned system will handle or exactly how it will respond when a driver fails to take over.

Several automakers already offer systems that reduce the work involved in highway driving. However, their capabilities vary considerably. Ford's BlueCruise allows hands-free driving on compatible roads, but drivers must continue paying attention. Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) can handle many driving tasks, although it still requires active human supervision.

Mercedes-Benz previously introduced its DRIVE PILOT system, which allowed conditional eyes-off driving in limited situations. However, the automaker has since pulled back from that technology in the U.S. as it develops its next generation of automated driving systems. GM's larger ambition is to make eyes-off driving available at highway speeds across a broader network of compatible roads. The company hopes to expand the capability to additional models after the Escalade IQ.

There's a financial incentive behind the push toward automated driving. Automakers increasingly offer advanced features through paid software subscriptions. GM already charges for continued Super Cruise access after the included service period expires. According to the company's August 2026 update, equipped vehicles include three years of service, followed by plans starting at $39.99 per month.

GM has not announced pricing for its future eyes-off technology. Some industry analysts believe drivers will be more willing to pay for technology that frees up their time behind the wheel. Still, there's a practical question for buyers. If you're already paying a premium for a luxury SUV, how much more would you be willing to spend each month to use its most advanced driving features?

WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK

If you're considering a vehicle with advanced driving technology, pay attention to what the manufacturer actually promises. Today's hands-free systems generally require you to keep watching the road. GM's planned eyes-off feature would allow you to look away only when the system is properly engaged under compatible conditions. Before paying for that capability, you'll want to know where it works and how the vehicle handles emergencies. It's also worth asking what happens if the system requests your attention while you're distracted.

Also, don't overlook the ongoing cost. Subscription fees could make a vehicle more expensive to own than its original purchase price suggests. And remember, GM's planned system remains under development. Until a manufacturer explicitly authorizes eyes-off operation under the appropriate conditions, keep watching the road and follow the system's instructions.

I love the idea of a less stressful drive, especially on those long stretches of highway where you're staring at the same traffic for miles. But handing over control is one thing. Taking my eyes off the road while traveling at highway speed is another. GM's research is encouraging because the company is studying how people actually behave when they're distracted. Still, I want to know what happens when the car encounters something it wasn't expecting. And if automakers plan to charge us every month for this technology, they'd better be able to show that it's safe and dependable. I'd be curious to try it, but I'd want a lot more evidence before settling in to watch a movie.

Would you trust your car enough to watch a movie while it drives at 70 mph, or would you always want to keep an eye on the road? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: College football corporate overlords ruin another classic rivalry game with stupid new name
item.description: The Florida-Georgia rivalry game has been rebranded as the "Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic" after moving to Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
The state of college football is in flux these days, to put it conservatively.

Between increasingly exorbitant NIL bills being footed by fans and boosters alike to an infinitely expanding College Football Playoff, the sport is going through its share of trials and tribulations.

One aspect of college football that has seemingly stood the test of time is the sanctity of the rivalry game (for the most part, anyway).

ESPN FUMBLES THE HOLY WAR BY FORCING UTAH AND BYU INTO A DREADED EARLY-MORNING KICKOFF FOR FANS

Sure, some great traditional showdowns have been railroaded thanks to the ever-evolving nature of the modern game, but most of the all-time exciting matchups in college football are safe.

The Game. The Iron Bowl. Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate. The Holy War.

These are games with names that have become synonymous with the sport, but lately, our corporate overlords have decided to screw with another tradition that is nearly universally loved by college fans.

The Florida Gators and Georgia Bulldogs play an annual rivalry game in the city of Jacksonville that is a sight to behold.

Orange and blue on one side, red and black on the other, split down the middle.

And for decades, they called this game "The World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party," and although both universities have distanced themselves from the moniker thanks to the negative implications of students drinking themselves blind at a football game (God forbid), the fans still use the name to this day.

Unfortunately, the game has been moved for the next few seasons thanks to renovations at EverBank Stadium, and a bunch of sponsors and suits saw this as an opportunity to rebrand one of the SEC's coolest rivalry games.

I'm sorry, the WHAT?

I can't believe they're going to make Chris Fowler and Kirk Herbstreit vomit out "The Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic" at the top of the broadcast.

I think I'm going to be sick.

Georgia fans and Florida fans can't agree on anything.

They don't agree on whether "Florida" or "Georgia" should come first when calling the game the "Florida-Georgia Game." They don't agree on the overall record in the series. And they can't even agree on who coined the term "Bloody Tuesday."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But one thing they all can agree on is that this name sucks.

What's even more insulting is the official Mercedes-Benz Stadium X account calling it a "cocktail party" in their social media caption, just reminding us what we lost.

I understand why they accepted a sponsorship to this game, and it's the same reason every terrible idea has been adopted in modern college football: money.

Oh, and by the way, just because EverBank Stadium is under renovations doesn't mean this game has to be played at another NFL venue.

These people are aware that the Gators and Bulldogs have on-campus stadiums, right?

It's not even an unprecedented event to have this game played in Athens or Gainesville, which happened in 1994 and 1995, respectively.

Two of the most iconic venues in the SEC will sit dormant this weekend so that a couple of corporate sponsors can milk some money out of a classic rivalry game.

You gotta love college sports in 2026!

item.title: UK charges 2 men in suspected Iran-linked incident at RAF Fairford after US bombers pulled
item.description: Two men face charges under the U.K.'s National Security Act after a September incident at RAF Fairford, a key base for U.S. military bombers.
item.content:encoded:
British prosecutors charged two men Tuesday under the U.K.’s National Security Act following an incident at RAF Fairford, a key base used by the U.S. military’s heavy bombers.

Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, of London, was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service. Nouman Essghir, 24, was charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom, according to the Crown Prosecution Service.

British counterterrorism police said they believe the foreign country Abdulkarim was assisting was Iran, Reuters reported.

RUBIO CONFIRMS 'FOREIGN ACTOR' INVOLVED IN UK TERROR PLOT

The charges follow a September incident near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England. British police arrested five men outside the base in the early hours of Sept. 27, according to Reuters.

The base had been used by U.S. bombers to carry out strikes against Iran. About a dozen B-1 bombers were among the aircraft later withdrawn from RAF Fairford and returned to their home stations in the United States on security grounds, according to previous Fox News reporting.

FOILED TERROR PLOT AT BOMBER BASE SIGNALS WIDER THREAT TO US MILITARY INSTALLATIONS: EXPERT

RAF Fairford serves as a key European operating location for U.S. heavy bombers and has supported American military missions.

Frank Ferguson, chief crown prosecutor for the CPS Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said the agency decided to prosecute the two men following a "complex" counterterrorism investigation.

"We will continue to work closely with our partners as this complex investigation continues," Ferguson said.

Both men were expected to appear Tuesday at Westminster Magistrates’ Court.

The CPS emphasized that the charges are not findings of guilt and that both defendants have the right to a fair trial.

item.title: Bill Maher, Justine Bateman compare far-left policies to 'The Purge in real life'
item.description: Justine Bateman and Bill Maher likened the DSA platform to horror movie "The Purge" in real life, questioning plans to abolish police, prisons, and the Senate.
item.content:encoded:
Actress Justine Bateman and comedian Bill Maher compared far-left policies — specifically, the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) goals — to "The Purge" in real life on Monday, questioning why critics of those policies are expected to "bow down."

"What's the endgame?" Bateman asked of the socialist policies of the DSA during an appearance on Maher's "Club Random" podcast. "Let's say you get everything you wanted. Let's say everything on that list. You get the whole thing. The whole thing. I mean, first of all, I can tell you for sure, anybody could tell you, you haven't thought this through."

Maher called it "cloud cuckoo land" as Bateman began comparing the proposals to the movie "The Purge."

DSA CO-CHAIR PUSHES BACK ON SOVIET UNION COMPARISONS, WANTS PRISONS TO BE 'LESS NECESSARY'

"You've got ‘The Purge’ in real life because you have no jails and no – everybody better have a gun. Don't touch the Second Amendment. Everybody needs a gun if you're going to have that," she said.

"I’ve said the same exact thing. It’s ‘The Purge.’ It’s ‘The Purge.’" 

"The Purge" is a movie about a government-sanctioned, 12-hour annual event where all crime, including murder, is completely legal.

BILL MAHER WARNS DEMOCRATS STILL HAVEN'T 'RENOUNCED THEIR CRAZY,' SAYS IT COULD SPELL TROUBLE IN 2028

"But again, as I said at the beginning, it's like you expect me to bow down to just one side of it, the left side of it. I'm the bad person because I'm questioning things," Maher said during the discussion with Bateman. "We're going to abolish the police, that everything is going to be free. I mean, their website literally says, 'Imagine this world where you don't have to worry about rent. You don't have to worry about transportation."

He continued, "But you're the good people. You're the smart people. You're the people who shouldn't be questioned."

The DSA did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

SOCIALISTS LAUNCH RADICAL PLATFORM TO ABOLISH THE US SENATE IN BID TO FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM AMERICA.

The DSA's policies drew scrutiny earlier this year after DSA co-chair Megan Romer discussed the organization's positions during an interview in July. Those positions included proposals to abolishing the Senate, police, and prisons.

Romer affirmed the organization's support for replacing the presidency and Supreme Court, abolishing ICE, eventually eliminating national borders while granting amnesty to people living in the country illegally, defunding the Pentagon, phasing out prisons and shifting most large corporations to public ownership during the interview.

BILL MAHER ADMITS HE COULD VOTE FOR JD VANCE, WARNS 'COWARDLY' DEMOCRATS FACE SOCIALIST TAKEOVER

"This is not about politics. This is about – and I was saying to the guys earlier, like to me, being an American is, I am free to pursue the kind of life I want and to do whatever I want so long as what I'm doing doesn't impinge on somebody else's ability to do the same. Now, the stuff they're talking about impinges on my ability. And this is not conducive to an American society," Bateman said.

Maher said he agreed and noted that he had told Vice President JD Vance in June that his vote was in play for Republicans if Democrats continued down this path.

"That's why I told the vice president, 'My vote is in play.' And then, of course, within 24 hours they wrote, 'Bill Maher is a Republican now.' I never said that. I'm not. I said my vote is in play," Maher said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Author, psychotherapist and cultural commentator Jonathan Alpert told Fox News Digital, "Here's a guy who's been a liberal his entire life, and now he's talking about voting Republican. That should tell Democrats something. He's not the one who's changed his politics dramatically. He's questioning how far some people on the left want to go."

"Bateman makes a good point," Alpert added. "What exactly happens if you get rid of police and prisons? Are we supposed to naively believe violent criminals will suddenly behave themselves? It's absurd to think you can just get rid of the institutions you don't like and somehow everything will work out. Human nature doesn't change because you pass a law. Maher and Bateman aren't asking anything outrageous. They're simply asking people to think through the consequences of what they're proposing. If you want to abolish prisons and police, you should be able to explain how you're going to keep people safe. That's not an unreasonable expectation."

item.title: Schumer, Dems are quietly betting big on one sleeper race in the Deep South
item.description: National Democrats reserved $1.2 million in Mississippi ads for Scott Colom as they target Cindy Hyde-Smith's Senate seat in a GOP stronghold.
item.content:encoded:
National Democrats are getting aggressive in the homestretch of this election cycle, sending money and party figureheads to a state that, for decades, has been out of reach.

Mississippi has been a Republican stronghold for the GOP in the Senate since the 1980s, but in a political environment that is proving tough for incumbents of the party in power, Democrats appear to smell blood in the water.

But Republicans aren’t buying the last-minute play in the Deep South, arguing that it’s a reach, at best, to make the race competitive.

DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS

"Largely, I think they’re just throwing s--- at the wall at this point," a GOP political operative told Fox News Digital.

The Senate Majority PAC, a political action committee with close ties to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., reserved $1.2 million in advertising in the state to boost Scott Colom, a district attorney mounting a bid against Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

And major figures in the Democratic Party, like former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, have also made the trip or are set to appear in the state — Buttigieg is scheduled to hold a rally on Mississippi’s Gulf Coast on Tuesday.

Jake Monssen, Hyde-Smith’s campaign manager, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "This is simply Washington insiders making a last-ditch effort to give life to Scott Colom's failing campaign."

"Scott is bankrolled by the radical left because he is in lockstep with their agenda," Monssen said. "He supports tax increases, open borders, taxpayer benefits for illegal immigrants, and sex change surgeries for minors."

Like in other races across the Senate map, Colom has a fight with history to contend with. Mississippi has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982, and the Magnolia State has consistently supported President Donald Trump.

TRUMP-BACKED SENATOR ADMITS GOP FACES NIGHTMARE SCENARIO IN STATE REPUBLICANS HAVEN'T LOST IN 90 YEARS

But Colom believes that the ground operation he’s developed while national Democrats stayed away from the state is what would put him over the top against Hyde-Smith, not the last-minute support.

"It could be enough," Colom told Fox News Digital. "I mean, the thing is, the people of Mississippi built this campaign."

Colom went on the offensive against Hyde-Smith, arguing that she "refuses to debate, she doesn’t campaign."

"Because of that, I was able to build momentum on the ground, which means now that it's getting attention, now that it's getting resources, I'm able to take advantage of it in a way that other candidates couldn't," he said.

Republicans aren’t resting on their laurels in the state, however. The Senate Leadership Fund, a political action committee closely aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., teed up a seven-figure ad buy there in response to Democrats’ spending.

And Trump appeared in Corinth, Mississippi, on Monday to rally for Hyde-Smith. He made a similar pitch to voters that he’s done at every rally stop this midterm cycle: pretend he’s on the ballot.

"In this election, if you would, I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot," Trump said. "And the reason is that when I'm on the ballot, exactly 49% more people show up."

Jonathan Klingler, a professor of political science at the University of Mississippi, told Fox News Digital that the increased spending and national attention to a once-sleepy race have generated the "talking point of Mississippi as evidence for momentum and building a Democratic wave."

THUNE MAKES BOLD PREDICTION ABOUT REPUBLICANS' SENATE CHANCES AS GOP PULLS MILLIONS FROM KEY RACES

"So at least I'm not — I can't say whether that's the intent of the funding here or visits, but that is the effect," he said.

There are also voter demographics that both Hyde-Smith and Colom have to contend with. Mississippi has the highest share of Black voters in the country at nearly 40% of the electorate. In order for Colom and "Democrats to be successful, they simply have to peel off a larger share of White voters," Klingler said.

There’s another storyline underneath the headlines of this race, too.

Hyde-Smith and Colom have a history dating back to the Biden administration, when the lawmaker blocked his nomination to serve as a district court judge in Mississippi.

"Instead of saving himself the embarrassment of being denied a job twice by Hyde-Smith, Colom is running a campaign backed by Chuck Schumer, funded by George Soros, and built on pro-transgender and other far-left policies," National Republican Senatorial Committee spokeswoman Bernadette Breslin told Fox News Digital.

That’s not Colom’s motivating factor, however. He had just left Trump's northeast Mississippi rally where he spoke to voters about their main concerns, "everybody I talked to, gas prices, grocery prices," and tariffs, he said.

But Colom said his personal dispute with Hyde-Smith was not his primary motivation.

"I'll tell you, as a Christian, I forgive her for that. That's not a motivating factor for me," Colom said. "I mean, as a district attorney, I have to prosecute cases where people lost their loved ones to gun violence. So, you know, and I’ve seen them forgive that person."

"So that's not the motivating factor," he continued. "For me, it's really the betrayal of the America First movement, right? Like she was supposed to help President Trump get lower grocery prices. Well, she betrayed us. We're not getting lower grocery prices."

item.title: Hit Netflix show boss, Obama’s former UN ambassador take shots at Trump's 'wreckage of our institutions'
item.description: "The Diplomat" showrunner Debora Cahn called 2025 Washington a "funeral," while Samantha Power slammed President Donald Trump's swift dismantling of USAID.
item.content:encoded:
Debora Cahn, showrunner of the Netflix series "The Diplomat," and former Obama United Nations Ambassador Samantha Power attacked the Trump administration on Monday amid cuts to the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID).

Cahn and Power took part in a discussion about the state of U.S. diplomacy and the series' latest season, along with the show's lead actress Keri Russell, at the John F. Kennedy Forum at Harvard. 

Throughout the event, they lamented the state of government since President Donald Trump took office again in 2025. Cahn described the situation in 2025 as a "funeral" in Washington.

"We go to Washington every year," Cahn said. "Last year, it was the funeral for democracy. I had never seen so many people in a state of complete existential despair over the wreckage that was falling around them, and I think we all went home and started Googling, 'How did you get an EU passport.'"

ELON MUSK THREATENS TO SUE RO KHANNA OVER CLAIMS USAID CUTS SENTENCED CHILDREN TO DEATH

However, she remarked that the upcoming midterm elections have provided more hope to people struggling in the "wreckage" of government institutions.

"I think as a citizen, I think we are all so exhausted by the constant barrage of, you know, somebody we talk to in Washington called them, 'dead cats getting thrown on the table' in the midst of the wreckage of our institutions," Cahn said.

"We no longer have the capacity for outrage. So, I worry we don't have the capacity to kind of mount any kind of resistance to the crumbling of our own democracy. And so, to see people are like, 'God, stop worrying about that, that is so last year. Move on. There are things we can do and things we will do.' It is good," she said.

Power took more issue with the Trump administration's dismantling of USAID, having been the agency's administrator from 2021-2025. She added that the truly "horrifying" part of the process was the compliance of the employees.

"For all of us who watched USAID be dismantled and other agencies in the U.S. government be gutted, what was so horrifying about it was the complacency and complicity of so many people who believed in that work five minutes before," Power said.

AP POST ON USAID CUTS BACKFIRES AS CRITICS QUESTION TAXPAYER-FUNDED NEPAL TRANSGENDER JOBS

"And the effectiveness of the people with the wrecking ball was that they did it so quickly and it really was shock and awe. And what it took away for so many, particularly those who worked at places like USAID, many of whom are here, was a sense of agency," she said.

Power lamented a lack of "dissent" within the president's team or from Congress, claiming it was a staple of the Biden administration.

"Whether it is the press, internal voices of debate even, not only dissent but even debate. Anything that is not just, 'Yes, Mr. President, what a brilliant idea, Mr. President,' that individual does not seem to get invited back to the next meeting. What does that result in? Not always, but chances are, really bad decisions, like invading a country on a false pretext and with no plan, in a manner that not only hurts the American people, the people of Iran and other countries but hurts the president," Power said.

She continued, "This is one thing that Liz Sherwood-Randall, who was President Biden's homeland security advisor, worked with me in the Obama administration. We were so fortunate that we had leaders who believe that dissent made and checks and balances and arguing things out made for better decisions in the end, even if it was really unpleasant, and they would have much preferred everybody to be like, 'Oh my God, what a great idea, Mr. President.'"

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and State Department for comment.

BILL GATES 'WORRIED' ABOUT SCALING BACK USAID: 'YOU COULD HAVE LITERALLY MILLIONS OF DEATHS'

Power has come under scrutiny for meeting with left-wing organizations during her time as a USAID administrator. 

According to nearly 700 pages of internal calendar entries obtained by Fox News Digital in 2023, Power met with George Soros' Open Society Foundations at least two times, the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation at least five times and held meetings with several other powerful groups like the Ford and Rockefeller foundations.

item.title: Kylian Mbappe predictably bends the knee after losing Chinese sponsors for laughing at meme of dictator Mao
item.description: Kylian Mbappe lost Chinese sponsors and saw Real Madrid matches banned on CCTV after laughing at a meme involving dictator Mao Zedong on TV.
item.content:encoded:
Soccer superstar Kylian Mbappe laughed at a meme involving Mao Zedong, the Chinese dictator who died a half-century ago, and is facing serious backlash in the form of losing Chinese sponsors and having his team's matches banned on television around the country.

During a recent interview on The Bridge, a French talk show hosted by Mbappe's Real Madrid teammate Aurelien Tchouameni, the 27-year-old star reportedly said the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator, they put my [face over it]." Mbappe smiled as the show cut to a meme of his face imposed on an image resembling Mao.

One of Mbappe's most popular nicknames is "The Dictator," given his prowess on the field and overall influence on the sport globally. Mao ruled China as a communist dictator from 1949 to 1976, with his regime resulting in tens of millions of deaths.

ADIDAS APOLOGIZES AFTER AD FEATURING FORMER ISRAELI SOLDIER WHO LOST LEG DRAWS BOYCOTT CALLS

Eastroc Beverage Group Co. and China Mengniu Dairy Co., two Chinese consumer brands that hired Mbappe, have both announced that they are cutting ties with Mbappe after their stocks took a hit, according to Bloomberg. Dongpeng, a drink company, stated it was cutting all ties with Mbappe as well.

Mbappe's official social media accounts on the Weibo and Xiaohongshu platforms have reportedly been frozen and marked with notices about violating regulations. State-run CCTV not only reportedly stopped airing Real Madrid matches in China, but also all La Liga matches, the top-flight league in Spain that features a total of 20 clubs.

Lin Jian, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry, even weighed in with a stark statement about Mbappe's joke about a meme. "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society," Jian stated, per The Financial Times.

With fierce action being taken by communist China, both La Liga and Mbappe did not take long to succumb to the pressure and swiftly issued apologies.

On Tuesday, La Liga issued a statement explaining that it "deeply regrets the offense caused by Kylian Mbappé's recent comments among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent LALIGA. To the extent of our institutional responsibility, we apologize on behalf of LALIGA and all its clubs."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Less than an hour later came Mbappe's apology, which he shared with his millions of followers across social media.

"During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself," the statement began. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.

"I apologise to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry."

If this situation feels familiar, it's because it is, as the NBA faced similar backlash in China years ago.

In 2019, then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey posted an image on Twitter, now X, showing support for pro-democracy protesters in Hong Kong. The image read, "Fight For Freedom. Stand With Hong Kong."

The backlash in China was swift and fierce, to put it mildly. The Rockets had many of their Chinese sponsors suspend ties with the organization, CCTV stopped broadcasting NBA games for roughly a year and league commissioner Adam Silver faced calls from the Chinese government that Morey should be fired.

Despite the NBA reportedly losing hundreds of millions of dollars as a result of Morey's post, Silver defended Morey's right to free speech while understanding the social media post offended some Chinese fans, and certainly the country's leaders.

LeBron James, however, took a different approach. As a Nike athlete with substantial financial ties to China, James claimed that Morey was "misinformed" by the situation taking place with the protests.

"And so many people could have been harmed not only financially, physically, emotionally, spiritually. So just be careful what we tweet and say and we do, even though, yes, we do have freedom of speech, but there can be a lot of negative that comes with that, too," James said when initially asked about the situation.

One year after his social media post, Morey resigned as the Rockets' general manager before quickly taking over as the president of basketball operations for the Philadelphia 76ers. Morey was fired by the 76ers in May 2026, two months before James opted to sign with Philadelphia.

item.title: Illinois man accused of threatening Congress with white substances in letters marked with his return address
item.description: Matthew Unglesbee allegedly told the FBI the white powder substance was salt and that he mailed the threatening letters to Congress as a joke.
item.content:encoded:
An Illinois man was charged with two felonies Monday after allegedly sending letters containing an unknown white powder substance to members of Congress, according to a criminal complaint.

Matthew G. Unglesbee was charged with false information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications after four members of Congress received the letters, which were marked with his return address, according to the complaint.

Unglesbee told the FBI the substance in the letters was salt and that he mailed them as a joke, the complaint read.

OHIO MAN CHARGED OVER GRAPHIC THREATS TO KILL TRUMP, BEHEAD GOP LAWMAKER

The FBI received a tip that Unglesbee had sent the letters on Oct. 16. The tipster had overheard Unglesbee at a restaurant saying he had mailed suspicious substances to members of Congress, the complaint stated.

The tipster allegedly provided authorities with Unglesbee’s full name, address and date of birth.

MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY POSTING GRUESOME DEATH THREATS AGAINST KRISTI NOEM, PAM BONDI ON SOCIAL MEDIA

Members of the FBI’s field office in Chicago responded to the offices of three members of Congress in the northern Illinois area after receiving the tip and a 911 call from one of the congressional offices.

"A staff member at Congressperson A's office, the first office to receive a letter, noticed that the letter felt like it contained a powder and the staffer could hear something inside the letter," the complaint read. This staff member called 911.

BIOWEAPON THREAT EXPOSED AS ANTHROPIC SOUNDS ALARM ON FOREIGN ACTORS PLOTTING VIRUS EXPERIMENTS

The office had already been on high alert, having received a similar letter within the previous few weeks, according to the complaint.

All three letters contained "a white granular substance" and a handwritten letter which read "HA HA," the complaint stated.

CONGRESS IS A HUGE TARGET FOR SPIES. MEMBERS AND STAFF NEED A WAKE-UP CALL AND TRAINING

On Friday, FBI Chicago responded to the office of a fourth member of Congress, a senator in the Northern District of Illinois. The senator had also received an envelope with a white granular substance, also with a letter which also read, "HAH enjoy the gift."

All four letters were marked with Unglesbee’s name and return address, according to the complaint.

FAA EMPLOYEE CHARGED WITH ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL PRESIDENT TRUMP IN EMAIL TO WHITE HOUSE

FBI Task Force Officer Chris Hobbs, who wrote the criminal complaint, characterized the letters as a common intimidation tactic, pointing out that preliminary lab testing "did not detect the presence of chemical or biological toxins in the white granular substance."

The FBI interviewed Unglesbee at his home Saturday when he allegedly confessed to sending the letters, telling law enforcement that he heard someone in a restaurant talking about similar letters Congress members had received.

UTAH MAN CHARGED WITH ATTEMPTED HATE CRIME AFTER ALLEGED THREAT TO 'BLOW UP' SYNAGOGUE

He told the FBI he knew his powder would be perceived as potentially being anthrax and anticipated people responding with hazmat suits.

He also told the FBI that the powder was salt, claiming he used salt specifically because it looked like anthrax.

PENNSYLVANIA MAN ACCUSED OF PLOTTING ISIS ATTACK ARRESTED WITH RIFLE AND 190 ROUNDS OF AMMUNITION: DOJ

"Unglesbee claimed he was joking but recognized that the recipients would not know he was joking and could perceive it as a threat," the complaint read.

The FBI searched Unglesbee's home and found a fifth letter marked with one of the congresspeople's Washington, D.C., office's address.

The FBI also determined that Unglesbee sent the letters on Oct. 19.

Fox News Digital contacted the FBI for further information.

item.title: Pakistan’s top court upholds Christian man’s death sentence for blasphemy
item.description: Pakistan’s Supreme Court upheld a Christian man’s death sentence for blasphemy in a historic ruling that advocates warn could have far-reaching consequences.
item.content:encoded:
Shock and anger greeted the Pakistani Supreme Court's decision to uphold the conviction and death sentence of a Christian man accused of blasphemy against the Prophet Muhammad. 

Supporters say the decision has far-reaching implications for human rights in Pakistan and for the country's standing on the international stage. The Open Doors 2026 World Watch List included the Asian nation in its top 10 list of countries where Christians face the most extreme persecution.

CeCe Heil, senior counsel and international legal director for the American Center for Law and Justice (ACLJ), told Fox News Digital the case against brothers Amoon and Qaisar Ayub began in 2014. 

AMERICANS TRAVEL TO PAKISTAN TO FREE CHRISTIANS TRAPPED IN MODERN-DAY SLAVERY: 'GOD'S HAND WAS IN IT'

Qaisar was arrested after a WordPress site displayed the Ayub brothers’ contact information and shared content that insulted the Prophet Muhammad. Amoon was arrested the following year. Heil says that in the 12 years of legal wrangling that followed, the Pakistani legal system has never presented evidence proving that either brother was truly affiliated with the offending WordPress blog site.

The ACLJ, through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), began representing Amoon shortly after his arrest in 2015. Both brothers were sentenced to death in 2018. They unsuccessfully sought appeal in the Lahore High Court in 2022. After a continuation at the Supreme Court in 2025, Qaisar asked the OLA to represent him.

Following years of arguments and 13 postponed hearings, an Oct. 7 verdict from the Supreme Court saw Amoon acquitted after some 10 years in prison, while Qaisar’s conviction and death sentence was upheld.

Heil said a threatening atmosphere now attends many blasphemy hearings, where she says "mobs" commonly show up in courtrooms.

In one trial, she said a mob filmed themselves saying that "if the judge does not enforce death by hanging, we will kill him by our own hands." She said another video shows a prominent lawyer involved in numerous blasphemy cases celebrating the 15-year journey that led to Qaisar’s sentencing. A translation of the description reads, "There is only one punishment for one who insults the Prophet: The death penalty for Qaisar Ayub."

Heil said the precedent set by the Supreme Court’s decision could impact "every single person that is sitting in prison right now on blasphemy charges," which includes at least three OLA clients.

Other Christian men facing death include Shahzad Masih, who was 16 years old when he was accused of blasphemy in 2017. He was sentenced to death five years later. His appeals have repeatedly been postponed since 2022.

Intizar Masih is awaiting trial for a blasphemous post he is said to have shared on WhatsApp in 2023. Ahsan Masih was accused of posting blasphemous content to TikTok in 2023, and was sentenced to death the following year. His appeal hearings have also been postponed.

The OLA plans to file a review petition with the Supreme Court as early as this week, addressing the lack of evidence convicting Qaisar. They also plan to reach out directly to the Government of Pakistan to request support, including a presidential pardon for Qaisar. 

Heil said she finds it "very strange" for a country posturing itself as a "more tolerant" negotiator between world powers in the ongoing conflict in Iran to fail to protect the religious freedoms of its people.

CHRISTIAN FARMING COMMUNITIES UNDER SIEGE AS US REPORT NAMES FULANI MILITANTS NIGERIA'S DEADLIEST THREAT

The Pakistani Embassy in Washington, D.C., did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about the possibility of a presidential pardon for Qaisar, or whether the Supreme Court’s decision could impact Pakistan’s perception in the West, or if justice can prevail in courtrooms mobbed with threatening onlookers.

A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the U.S. "is concerned about religious freedom in Pakistan and throughout the world" and "we regularly discuss this concern with Pakistan, as we would with any country."

Heil said the ACLJ has requested that Morris Tidball-Binz, the United Nations special rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, intercede on Qaisar’s behalf.

Tidball-Binz did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about whether he held concerns about the precedent set by the Supreme Court upholding Qaisar’s conviction.

The Human Rights Council secretariat provided a letter that Tidball-Binz and other U.N. officials wrote to the Government of Pakistan in September 2025, emphasizing their concerns about the cases of the Ayub brothers and Shahazad Masih. 

It stated, "Without making any judgment as to the accuracy of the information made available to us, we would like to express our grave concern about the imposition of the mandatory death penalty for blasphemy related charges against Mr. Shahzad Masih, Mr. Qaiser Ayub and Mr. Amoon Ayub, despite an apparent lack of conclusive evidence against them for acts and for offenses which do not qualify as ‘most serious crimes.’"

The U.N. officials concluded, "If the above allegations prove to be accurate, they would be in contravention of Mr. Shahazad Masih´s, Mr. Qaiser Ayub’s and Mr. Amoon Ayub’s rights to life, not to be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, not to be deprived arbitrarily of their liberty and to be afforded fair proceedings before an independent and impartial tribunal, to freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief, the right to express their opinion in a peaceful manner and the right to be equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law without any discrimination." 

The Government of Pakistan responded earlier this year, and outlined how "Under Pakistan's Constitution, such matters fall within the judicial domain, and the Executive is constitutionally prohibited from intervening in individual cases."

Heil said that while Amoon has been spared from the death penalty, their work is ongoing to keep him safe from reprisals.

item.title: Kamala Harris calls Trump administration 'most callous and corrupt' in American history
item.description: Kamala Harris called the Trump White House the "most callous and corrupt" administration in history while campaigning for David Crowley in Wisconsin.
item.content:encoded:
While on the campaign trail Monday for Democrats ahead of the midterms, former Vice President Kamala Harris offered some of her harshest criticism of the Trump White House yet, calling it the "most callous and corrupt and incompetent" presidential administration in American history.

Twice during her speech at an event for David Crowley, the Democratic nominee for governor in Wisconsin, Harris accused the Trump administration of wielding an agenda of "brutality" against Americans.

Though in her lambasting of President Donald Trump's character and leadership style, she didn't mention him by name once.

"We in this room, I know, understand that the measure of the strength of the leader is based on who you lift up, not who you beat down," Harris said. "Unlike some other people who are constantly looking in the mirror, David is looking at the people. That's the kind of leader we want."

KAMALA HARRIS CLAIMS GOP 'CHEATING' AHEAD OF MIDTERMS, SAYS SHE'S FOCUSED ON STOPPING THE 'MADNESS'

Her more specific, policy-based attacks came against Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Wis., Crowley's opponent in the gubernatorial race.

Harris noted that Tiffany supported Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020 election based on unsubstantiated claims of widespread fraud, before framing the upcoming election as a test of longstanding democratic norms.

"Let's talk about the fact that David's opponent denied the election of 2020. By the way, we won. Yes, you can call me former madam Vice President. We won that election," Harris said.

She continued: "We are now in the phase of the moment in our democracy, while we can still hold on to it, where the people's voice reigns, where the will of the people reigns, where the power of the people is demonstrated by what we do to organize."

MAPPED: THE STATES TRUMP AND TOP DEMOCRATS ARE TARGETING BEFORE ELECTION DAY

At an earlier event on Monday, Crowley called Harris a "huge mentor" of his, adding that his wife loves her.

Tiffany pounced on the connection in a social media post, accusing Crowley of sharing Harris' support for higher taxes, "taxpayer benefits for illegals" and "Green New Deal policies" that he argued would drive up energy costs.

Over the last several weeks, Harris has barnstormed through several key presidential battlegrounds to campaign alongside Democrats, including Nevada gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford and Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Chris Pappas in New Hampshire.

Her increased involvement has only fueled speculation that she is laying the groundwork for another White House run in 2028.

During a September event with NAACP leaders in Detroit, Harris said she has yet to decide whether she'll run for president again.

"I do sincerely believe '28 won't matter if we don't get through '26," she said.

The comedian, who stars in the upcoming holiday horror film "Christmas at the Kringles," told Fox News Digital that getting a job in the city is more the exception than the rule now.

"I think a lot has changed, the way things are done," he explained. "I used to be out here because I needed to be available to work here. A lot of the work isn't here anymore. I mean, a lot of it, the work is not here anymore. It's the exception now, if you get to work here. So that's one reason."

item.title: COREY BROOKS: Chicago schools are failing kids at the one skill that can change their lives
item.description: Only 23% of Chicago fourth graders scored proficient on the 2024 Nation's Report Card, exposing a literacy crisis with devastating consequences.
item.content:encoded:
In Chicago, one of America’s prized and wealthiest cities, only 23% of its fourth graders scored proficient or higher in reading on the 2024 National Assessment of Educational Progress, which is also known as the Nation’s Report Card. Another 53% scored below basic.

That means that three out of four fourth-graders could not demonstrate solid command of reading skills, and more than half lacked even partial mastery. What is even worse is that the increase in reading proficiency from fourth to eighth grade was only four percentage points—from 23% to 27%. Despite having these damning statistics before them, the educators and parents raised no alarms—those who improved were the exception to the rule.

I have discussed youth literacy in previous Rooftop Revelations, and it remains the most pressing issue for the youth I serve. There are real humans behind these test scores. And you will notice that I did not bring race into this issue yet. Those numbers are for all of Chicago’s students. We are all affected by this decline in education standards.

MCMAHON CALLS FOR 'RESET' OF EDUCATION AFTER US SPENT $3 TRILLION AND STILL SAW READING SCORES DECLINE

A child who cannot read proficiently by the end of third grade is four times more likely to fail to graduate from high school on time than a proficient reader. The number is even worse for children who live in poverty. What kind of quality of life can these children expect as adults? We know from common sense that adults with limited literacy face higher unemployment and lower earnings over their lifetimes. They are literally shut out of any job that requires literacy as a skill.

I see the damage from this illiteracy epidemic on the South Side of Chicago every day. I see young people who cannot fill out a simple job application. They come by my church for help. I see it in parents who cannot read medical reports that determine what help their children receive. I have even had to help people who graduated from high school without being able to read and cannot read a lease or understand a text message from a supervisor. 

No American should need help with these simple tasks in 2026, and it is no wonder why so many stay trapped in the same cycle of poverty or end up in prison. Reading is the one skill that opens the door to the wider world. Reading can lift anyone from poverty, for it is a skill that enriches the reader with knowledge, spirit and know-how. Without this skill, how can one pursue economic opportunity, personal freedom and one’s dreams?

AMERICA’S MASSIVE LABOR CRISIS STARTED IN THE CLASSROOM, NOT THE WORKPLACE

This high level of illiteracy is a disease within our city, and yet we treat it like background noise. We give so many other issues, like homelessness and immigration, a higher priority than reading. I’m not discounting those issues at all. I am simply making the point that this illiteracy crisis should rank up there, but it doesn’t. And that is why we continue to fail over and over on the one skill that gives children the real key to a better future: the ability to read.

I have kids of my own, and I am a very busy man with a congregation that depends on me at all hours of the day, but I know that teaching a child to read is not complicated. 

The science of reading has been settled for decades. It starts with phonics. Each letter is sounded out, and we teach the kids how to blend those sounds into words. We do this at home every night before bedtime, when we read to our children and then challenge them to sound out the words back to us. 

We do this every day, and schools that use these structured literacy programs see results. But somewhere along the way, our schools decided that the fundamentals were too simple, that children needed something more sophisticated than learning to sound out words. They were wrong. The children paid for it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

We must put the blame where it belongs, and most of it belongs at the feet of the parents. Do not have a child if you do not have the time to read to him or her every night before bed. There are no excuses for that. 

I blame the schools that pass along kids to the upper grades when they cannot read at grade level. Anybody who says that these kids are our future and does not stress reading is part of the problem. We must become merciless in our pursuit of literacy, and there should be no excuses.

That is why I am working to open my own school alongside the Leadership and Economic Opportunity Center. I believe this school will set a new standard in this community, one where academic excellence is not the exception but the expectation. We will teach parents how to read to their children every night. When they see what it does for their kids, they will tell other parents. That is how a movement starts. When children arrive at kindergarten already knowing their sounds and their letters, their teachers will see what is possible and want more of it. 

I believe this can change the spirit of our community from the ground up. I can envision it. I am building it.

item.title: Retired Navy admiral warns of decades-long UAP 'cover-up,' points to deep ocean as ultimate hiding spot
item.description: Retired Rear Adm. Tim Gallaudet tells Sean Hannity why the deep ocean's vast unexplored depths could be the ultimate UAP hiding place today.
item.content:encoded:
A retired Navy rear admiral is pulling back the curtain on what he believes is an 80-year government UFO cover-up, explaining why the deep ocean could be the ultimate hiding place for unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAPs).

"If they were to go somewhere basically to not be detected for a period of time ... where would you want to go?" retired Rear Adm. Tim Gallaudet asked Sean Hannity on his "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast.

"You'd want to go ... [to] the most unexplored area of the world, and that's the ocean."

RETIRED NAVY ADMIRAL MAKES BOMBSHELL CLAIM ABOUT UFOS AND 'NON-HUMAN INTELLIGENCE' CONTROLLING THEM

Gallaudet, a former acting administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), appeared on Tuesday's episode of the podcast discussing the mysteries of the deep ocean and what could lurk beneath the surface.

His decades of experience studying the ocean have led him to question what its depths could contain, particularly given how much of the seafloor remains unmapped, according to ocean-mapping researchers.

HARVARD ASTRONOMER TAPPED TO LEAD WHITE HOUSE UFO COUNCIL SAYS US GOVERNMENT 'BAFFLED BY WHAT THEY ARE SEEING'

"We've only explored with either drones, buoys, floats, about 10% of ocean volume," Gallaudet said. "So there's a lot of mystery out there right now."

His remarks come as Navy personnel have reported encounters with unidentified objects that they say can travel between air and water without any apparent disturbance.

Gallaudet described a video that he said shows a mysterious object moving rapidly underwater before emerging from the water without disturbing the surface, hovering briefly and then accelerating skyward.

"It goes into the ocean, no disturbance," Gallaudet said.

"I'm aware of another video that shows something similar, but from overhead ... so yeah, there's something that they've been able to engineer that we have no idea how to reproduce," he added.

Gallaudet also described the objects as silent, saying they can accelerate beyond the speed of sound without producing a sonic boom — a capability he suggested would be difficult to explain using known technology.

Beyond the mysterious sightings, Gallaudet and Hannity also discussed claims that the government has attempted to recover and study craft of non-human origin, accusations of decades-long government secrecy surrounding UAP encounters and efforts to increase transparency about the U.S. government's knowledge of unidentified phenomena.

Viewers and listeners can watch or listen to Gallaudet's full conversation with Hannity on "Hang Out with Sean Hannity," available on YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts and iHeartRadio.

FBI SEIZES SWALWELL’S DEVICES AT AIRPORT AS SEXUAL MISCONDUCT INVESTIGATION ESCALATES: SOURCES
